values.goal: Use the Composition API to distinguish state, derived values, and side effects, and manage the lifetimes of notes and Canvas.
values.capstone: A Vue workspace with per-unit notes and Canvas, a props/emits contract table, a React lifetime comparison, and resource audit records.

values.title: Reactivity and Templates
values.prerequisites: JavaScript objects, arrays, and functions; HTML forms; running an npm project.
values.environment: Use .vue SFCs and script setup in a separate Vue Vite project. Record package versions and the lockfile, and run on the development server. The built-in Vue examples use the h function and are not a general-purpose SFC compiler. The existing vue-01 preview is a starting point. Implement the extended deliverables described here in a separate project.
values.concepts.0.title: ref
values.concepts.0.explanation: ref wraps a reactive value, which you read and write with .value in scripts. Templates automatically unwrap top-level refs for display.
values.concepts.1.title: computed
values.concepts.1.explanation: computed calculates a result from the reactive values it reads. Do not copy values derivable from the source, such as the completed count, into another ref.
values.outcomes.0: The completed count increases by 1 per toggle.
values.outcomes.1: The original 3 cards remain after removing the filter.
values.steps.0: In script setup in src/App.vue of an external Vue Vite project, create a ref containing 3 cards.
values.steps.1: Use computed to derive the completed count and incomplete list, and display them in the template.
values.steps.2: Connect the completion button and record how the list and total change together in notes/day01.md.
values.variables.0.name: Completed cards
values.variables.0.expected: The completed count is 1 and the incomplete list contains 2 cards.
values.criteria.0: The completed count increases by 1 per toggle.
values.criteria.1: The original 3 cards remain after removing the filter.
values.questions.0: Why does ref access differ between scripts and templates?
values.questions.1: What cost does copying the completed count with watch introduce?
values.references.0.title: Vue Reactivity Fundamentals
values.references.1.title: Vue Composition API Guide

values.title: SFCs and Template Binding
values.prerequisites: Unit 2 builds on the work and experiment records from Unit 1.
values.environment: First check the execution scope guidance on the example screen. The following is the preparation environment for extending the assignment in a separate project. Use .vue SFCs and script setup in a separate Vue Vite project. Record package versions and the lockfile, and run on the development server. The built-in Vue examples use the h function and are not a general-purpose SFC compiler.
values.concepts.0.title: SFC
values.concepts.0.explanation: A .vue file compiles its template, logic, and styles into one component. Distinguish runtime h function examples from SFCs that require a build.
values.concepts.1.title: Binding
values.concepts.1.explanation: v-bind passes an expression result to an attribute. String attributes and dynamic boolean attributes have different meanings in the browser.
values.outcomes.0: The button can be clicked with a false binding.
values.outcomes.1: The button is disabled with a true binding.
values.steps.0: Write script setup and template in src/Card.vue.
values.steps.1: Bind :disabled and :aria-pressed to the completion state.
values.steps.2: Compare a fixed disabled string with a boolean binding and record the DOM attributes.
values.variables.0.name: disabled value
values.variables.0.expected: Whether the button can actually be operated changes.
values.criteria.0: The button can be clicked with a false binding.
values.criteria.1: The button is disabled with a true binding.
values.questions.0: Why can disabled='false' disable a button?
values.questions.1: Why does an SFC file fail to run in a general JS runner?
values.references.0.title: Vue Reactivity Fundamentals
values.references.1.title: Vue Composition API Guide

values.title: reactive and Preserving References
values.prerequisites: Unit 3 builds on the work and experiment records from Unit 2.
values.environment: First check the execution scope guidance on the example screen. The following is the preparation environment for extending the assignment in a separate project. Use .vue SFCs and script setup in a separate Vue Vite project. Record package versions and the lockfile, and run on the development server. The built-in Vue examples use the h function and are not a general-purpose SFC compiler.
values.concepts.0.title: reactive
values.concepts.0.explanation: reactive creates a Proxy that tracks object property access. Destructuring a reactive object into plain values can break the connection.
values.concepts.1.title: Choosing ref
values.concepts.1.explanation: ref suits a single value, including replacement of an object. If you need to pass object properties separately, consider a connection mechanism such as toRefs.
values.outcomes.0: The linked query matches the original input.
values.outcomes.1: Reproduce how ordinary destructuring retains the initial value.
values.steps.1: Display the destructured query and the query obtained through toRefs separately.
values.steps.2: Change the original query through the input and record the difference between the two displays.
values.variables.0.name: Property extraction
values.variables.0.expected: Only the display linked through toRefs follows changes to the source.
values.criteria.0: The linked query matches the original input.
values.criteria.1: Reproduce how ordinary destructuring retains the initial value.
values.questions.0: Which is more convenient, reactive or ref, when you must replace the entire object?
values.questions.1: Are nested properties tracked in the same way?
values.references.0.title: Vue Reactivity Fundamentals
values.references.1.title: Vue Composition API Guide
